title: Retention SDK and CI linter for prompt/response lifecycle
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Problem statement: Customers frequently ask for guardrails that prevent accidental long-term storage of prompts, model responses and request logs. Currently retention configuration lives in the Console and API but is set post-deployment, which makes it hard for product teams to ensure library-level defaults and CI validation are enforced across large codebases.

Goal: Deliver a lightweight Retention SDK plus a CI linter and pre-commit hook that lets engineers encode retention expectations in their code and CI pipelines, enforces allowed TTL ranges at build-time, and generates an audit-ready export manifest for evidence requests. This reduces misconfiguration risk, speeds audits, and provides traceable policy-to-code mappings.

Scope:
- Retention SDK (Node/Python): helper methods to set per-request TTLs for prompts/responses, annotate requests with retention-class and justification metadata, and fallback to tenant/default policies if omitted.
- CI linter (CLI): static analysis that scans repository calls to Redwood client APIs and flags usages that set TTL outside allowed bounds (e.g., >365 days, or missing justification when >30 days). Configurable rules per repo via .retentionrc.
- Pre-commit hook: optional hook that surfaces linter failures locally and offers automated fixes (e.g., insert standard justification comment or replace explicit large TTL with constant).
- Evidence manifest generator: CLI/SDK helper that produces a signed manifest mapping code locations, runtime configuration, and request sampling policy for an exported evidence bundle. Manifest format is JSON-LD compatible and contains human-readable links to source files and deployment identifiers.

Out of scope for this ticket: runtime enforcement inside the private control plane (handled by ENG tickets), server-side retention simulator UI changes (separate PM), and migration tooling for historical logs > TTL.

Success metrics:
- 80% of newly onboarded customers install the linter or pre-commit within their first 30 days of using the SDK.
- Reduce accidental >90-day retention misconfigurations surfaced in support incidents by 60% in Q2 after launch.
- Evidence manifest accepted by at least one enterprise SOC audit without follow-up questions.

Acceptance criteria:
1) SDK provides clear APIs to set per-request TTL and retention-class in both Node and Python, with docs and examples.
2) Linter scans JS/TS/Python and flags (a) missing TTL, (b) TTLs above tenant-max defined in .retentionrc, (c) missing justification when TTL > configured threshold.
3) Pre-commit hook installed via standard package managers and documented in onboarding template.
4) Evidence manifest generator emits a signed manifest that includes: service name, git commit, file locations, request sampling policy, and retention rules applied.
5) End-to-end sample repo demonstrating linter, SDK usage, and manifest generation exists in /redwood-examples/retention-sdk.
6) Developer docs and one migration/FAQ page describing how to adopt the SDK and best practices.

Rollback and rollout plan: staged release. Beta to internal platform team + 3 pilot customers for two weeks, gather feedback, then wide release. Provide opt-out flag in Console until enforcement is generally adopted.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Linter false positives annoy developers. Mitigation: provide whitelisting rules and an interactive autofix.
- Risk: Manifest format rejection by compliance teams. Mitigation: iterate with a pilot SOC contact and include export schema versioning.

Notes: this ticket coordinates with ENG for server-side API support (ENG-32411) and traceability headers (ENG-32790). Linked design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SEC/Retention+SDK+and+Manifest (draft). Example PR for SDK bootstrap: https://github.com/redwood-inference/retention-sdk/pull/7
